comparison.objective: Commission and lock a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative dynamic-impact tuning; the record instead lowers/refits a glovebox and replaces a cabin filter.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew unlocking/relocking, fine collar rotation, counterholding, bounded torque, and response-guided adjustment. The record requires simultaneous sprung-panel squeezing, hinged closure, filter extraction, regrasping, and keyed-slot insertion. Shared bimanual handling is only generic.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable physical carriage stops within a 12 mm stroke at ≥0.85 J, without hard-stop contact, excess rebound, overload, or lock drift. The record requires staged glovebox lowering, old-filter removal, new-filter seating within position/orientation tolerances, and glovebox relatching for 1 s. Candidate omits numeric thresholds for excessive rebound, overload, and collar-drift tolerance, but those omissions do not plausibly duplicate the unrelated filter-replacement rubric.
comparison.reason: All three axes test meaningfully different abilities: closed-loop damper commissioning and retention under dynamic impacts versus access-panel manipulation and keyed consumable replacement. Different hardware is not the basis of the verdict; the manipulation sequence, feedback dependency, and terminal physics are different.
